 Search 11 New K-Dramas Premiering in November 2026 That K-Drama Fans Can’t Miss
 Disha Paul 5 minutes ago 8 min read K-drama fans, get your winter watchlists ready! November 2026 is bringing a busy release schedule, with fantasy romance, supernatural love stories, workplace comedies, historical battles, and crime thrillers arriving throughout the month. 
 There is something for almost every mood, whether you want an intense story to binge or a comforting romance to watch after a long day. 
 Your November watchlist is about to get BUSY! From heart-fluttering romance to revenge-fueled drama and plot twists you won't see coming, these 11 new K-dramas deserve a spot on your radar. Which one will become your next obsession? The lineup also includes several highly anticipated adaptations and returning dramas. The Remarried Empress brings a beloved fantasy story to live action, Good Partner returns with a new professional partnership, and Crash brings its traffic crime investigation team back for another round of action. 
 With 11 titles on the list, fans will have plenty to choose from as the year draws to a close. Here are the November 2026 K-dramas, arranged by their reported premiere dates, along with their casts, episode counts, and streaming platforms. 
 1. The Remarried Empress 
 The Remarried Empress (Disney+) The Remarried Empress is one of November's major fantasy romance releases. Based on the popular web novel and webtoon, the live-action adaptation follows Navier ( Shin Min-a ), an empress whose seemingly perfect marriage falls apart when her husband, Emperor Sovieshu ( Ju Ji-hoon ), falls for another woman. 
 Rather than allowing her divorce to destroy her position, Navier makes an unexpected decision. She agrees to the separation but requests permission to marry Heinrey ( Lee Jong-suk ), a prince from a rival kingdom. Her choice sets the stage for palace politics, complicated relationships, and a fight to reclaim control over her future. 
 Aired: November 4, 2026 
 No. of Episodes:  10 
 Cast:   Shin Min-a , Ju Ji-hoon , Lee Jong-suk , Lee Se-young 
 Streaming Platform:  Disney+, Hulu 
 2. Next Seat, Francesca 
 Next Seat, Francesca (Wavve) What happens when a vampire has to fit into an ordinary high school? Next Seat, Francesca brings a supernatural twist to a teen romance, following Pi Na-young ( Han Su-a ), a vampire who transfers to a school after arriving from Romania. 
 Na-young must keep her identity hidden while adjusting to human life. Her situation becomes more complicated when she meets Jang Woo-joo ( Kim Hyun-jin ), a model student and class president who dreams of attending medical school. As he helps her settle into school, their connection begins to grow. 
 The series expands the universe of the 2005 sitcom Hello, Francesca , reworking its vampire premise for a younger audience. With its mix of secret identities, school life, and forbidden romance, it offers a lighter supernatural option among November's releases. 
 Aired: November 6, 2026 
 No. of Episodes:  4 
 Cast:   Han Su-a , Kim Hyun-jin , Lee Seung-gyu , with special appearances by Chung Seung-je and Yoo Young-woo 
 Streaming Platform:  Wavve 
 3. One-of-a-Kind Romance 
 One of a Kind Romance (TVING) One-of-a-Kind Romance brings together an ordinary job seeker and a famous actor whose lives become unexpectedly connected. Gong Yu-il ( Joy ) is trying to build a career while juggling part-time jobs, but her plans take an unusual turn when she encounters top star Tak Mu-i ( Kim Hyun-jin ). 
 Yu-il finds herself becoming Mu-i's manager. Mu-i is a celebrity whose public image hides the anxiety and emotional scars left by stalking. Their relationship develops through a shared interest in a novel, giving them a connection beyond the usual celebrity-and-manager dynamic. 
 Adapted from a webtoon, the drama combines the excitement of a celebrity romance with a more personal story about trust and emotional healing. Joy's return to acting is another reason fans may want to keep this series on their radar. 
 Aired: November 9, 2026 
 No. of Episodes:  12 
 Cast:   Joy (Park Soo-young), Kim Hyun-jin , Shin Hyun-soo , Kang Na-eon 
 Streaming Platform:  TVING in South Korea; international availability varies by region 
 4. Happy Anding 
 Happy Anding (tvN) Not every K-drama needs a murder mystery or a complicated love triangle to keep viewers interested. Happy Anding , also known as Life's Punchline , focuses on three aspiring comedians trying to find their place in a difficult industry. 
 The story follows performers who share a passion for comedy but must face the gap between their ambitions and reality. Their journey involves unsuccessful attempts, personal setbacks, and the gradual process of learning what it takes to keep pursuing a dream. 
 Based on the Japanese drama Life's Punchline , the series could appeal to viewers who enjoy character-driven stories about friendship, creative ambition, and the uncertain years spent trying to establish a career. 
 Aired: November 6, 2026 
 No. of Episodes:  12 
 Cast:   Kang Hoon , Cho Hyun-chul , Kim Jung-jin 
 Streaming Platform:  tvN in South Korea; international streaming platform not confirmed 
 5. What a Boss Wants 
 What a Boss Wants (MBN) What a Boss Wants adds an unusual premise to November's romance lineup. Kwon Do-hyuk ( Sung Hoon ), an entertainment company CEO, has built a life around control and success. Yet he becomes fascinated by a mysterious singer whose voice has brought him comfort during difficult moments. 
 Lee Eun-chae ( Oh Se-young ), the lead vocalist of an indie band, becomes the focus of Do-hyuk's search. When he discovers a clue that connects her to the music he has been searching for, he sets out to meet her. Their encounters gradually become more personal, but Eun-chae has secrets of her own. 
 Aired: November 11, 2026 
 No. of Episodes:  12 
 Cast:   Sung Hoon , Oh Se-young 
 Streaming Platform:  MBN in South Korea; international platform TBA 
 6. Sword & Silence 
 Sword & Silence (KBS2) For viewers who prefer political struggles and large-scale battles, Sword & Silence brings a historical epic to the November lineup. Also known as The Great King Munmu, the drama tells the story of Silla's efforts to unite the Three Kingdoms of Korea during a period of fierce conflict. 
 Kim Yu-sin ( Park Sung-woong ) is a celebrated general, while Kim Beop-min ( Lee Hyun-wook ) is a key royal figure who later becomes King Munmu. Kim Chun-chu ( Kim Kang-woo ) also plays an important role in the political and military struggle. 
 The story follows the difficult alliances and military campaigns that shape the kingdom's future. Beyond the battlefield, the characters must manage competing loyalties and the pressure of leading a kingdom through a period of major change. 
 Aired: November 14, 2026 
 No. of Episodes:  28 
 Cast:   Jang Hyuk , Lee Hyun-wook , Park Sung-woong , Kim Kang-woo 
 Streaming Platform:  KBS2 in South Korea; international platform TBA 
 7. Crash 2: Fury Road 
 Crash 2 (Disney+) The Traffic Crime Investigation team returns, and this time its cases expand beyond its original local setting. Crash 2: Fury Road continues the story of the team that investigates dangerous traffic-related crimes, combining police work with fast-paced action and humor. 
 Cha Yeon-ho ( Lee Min-ki ) returns as a highly analytical investigator, alongside Min So-hee ( Kwak Sun-young ), whose driving and investigative skills make her a valuable member of the team. Heo Sung-tae and Lee Ho-cheol also return as members of the investigation unit. 
 The new season brings the team into a larger investigative structure, where increasingly serious offenders present new challenges. 
 Aired: November 16, 2026 
 No. of Episodes:  12 
 Cast:   Lee Min-ki , Kwak Sun-young , Heo Sung-tae , Lee Ho-cheol , Moon Hee , Park Ji-sung 
 Streaming Platform:  Disney+ 
 8. Good Partner 2 
 Good Partner 2 (SBS) Good Partner is returning with a new chapter in the professional life of divorce lawyer Cha Eun-kyung ( Jang Na-ra ). After establishing her own law firm, she is ready to take on another set of difficult cases and work with a new colleague. 
 Jang Na-ra reprises her role as Eun-kyung, while Kang Hye-sung ( Kim Hye-yoon ) joins the second season as a lawyer. Their partnership brings a new dynamic to the series, with both women bringing different experiences and approaches to the cases they handle. 
 The new season will continue exploring the personal consequences of divorce, but it will also look at what happens after the legal battle ends. That gives the drama room to examine clients' decisions, family relationships, and the professional challenges facing its lawyers. 
 Aired: November 20, 2026 
 No. of Episodes:  11, according to current listings 
 Cast:   Jang Na-ra , Kim Hye-yoon , P.O , and returning supporting cast members 
 Streaming Platform:  SBS in South Korea; international availability varies by region 
 9. The Blue Road 
 The Blue Road (Netflix) The Blue Road brings an international investigation to Netflix, pairing South Korean and Japanese detectives in a case involving a series of disturbing murders. 
 The story begins when investigators discover bodies accompanied by messages written in different languages. As similar crimes emerge in both Japan and South Korea, the authorities realise that the cases may be connected. The investigation forces detectives from Seoul and Tokyo to work together, following clues that cross national borders. 
 Son Suk-ku and Eita Nagayama lead the series, bringing together two actors from different entertainment industries in a tense crime thriller. 
 Aired: November 20, 2026 
 No. of Episodes:  8 
 Cast:   Son Suk-ku , Eita Nagayama , Kim Shin-rok , Choi Sung-eun , Jung Jae-young 
 Streaming Platform:  Netflix 
 10. The Substitute 
 The Substitute (TVING) The Substitute is one for fans of darker school dramas. Directed by Park So-yeon, who also directed Pyramid Game , the upcoming thriller turns academic pressure into the centre of a dangerous arrangement between students. 
 Nam Jae-yeob ( Bae Hyun-sung ) appears to have the perfect life, with wealth, good grades, and the image of an ideal student. Kang Geon-tae ( Cha Kang-yoon ) is a scholarship student whose academic success represents a chance to build a better future. 
 When Jae-yeob discovers Geon-tae's weakness, he blackmails him into taking a university entrance exam on his behalf. The arrangement puts Geon-tae's ambitions at risk and creates a conflict in which secrets and manipulation could have serious consequences. 
 Aired: November 23, 2026 
 No. of Episodes:  10, according to current listings 
 Cast:   Bae Hyun-sung , Cha Kang-yoon , Park Yoon-ho , Uhm Ji-won , Park Hyuk-kwon , Baek Ji-won 
 Streaming Platform:  TVING 
 11. Nine to Six 
 Still from Nine to Six K-drama (SBS) Closing out the month is Nine to Six , a workplace romance about a woman who has spent years prioritising her career and a younger man whose warmth challenges her carefully organised life. 
 Kang Yi-ji ( Park Min-young ) is a dedicated professional who approaches work with logic and discipline but finds romance much harder to manage. Her routine changes when she meets Han Seon-woo ( Yook Sung-jae ), a kind-hearted younger man who joins her working world. 
 Go Soo also stars as Park Hyun-tae, a capable general manager who evaluates employees according to their performance. The office setting brings professional expectations, difficult colleagues, and personal relationships into the same story. 
 Aired: November 25, 2026 
 No. of Episodes:  12 
 Cast:   Park Min-young , Yook Sung-jae , Go Soo , Joo Hyun-young , Kim Mi-kyung 
 Streaming Platform:  Prime Video 
 Which November 2026 K-Drama Should You Watch First? 
 With so many genres arriving in the same month, choosing just one may be difficult. Fantasy romance fans can start with The Remarried Empress , while viewers looking for a supernatural love story can try Next Seat, Francesca . One of a Kind Romance and Nine to Six offer different takes on romance, and Happy Anding brings a more grounded story about chasing a creative dream. 
 For a darker watch, The Substitute and The Blue Road offer crime-driven suspense, while Crash 2: Fury Road brings back action and investigation. Sword & Silence is the choice for viewers who prefer historical battles, and Good Partner 2 returns to the legal world with new professional challenges. 
 November's lineup offers plenty of ways to spend the colder evenings, whether you prefer a comforting romance or a tense mystery. With these dramas arriving throughout the month, fans can start planning their watchlists now. 
 Which November 2026 K-drama are you most excited to watch first?
